ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, as amended (Articles 4, 5 and 45), and its Enforcement Decree; Real Name Financial Transactions Act (Article 3-2); Commercial Act (Articles 289, 290, 292, 297, 300, 317, 318 and 330); Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service AML/CFT administrative guidance on customer due diligence and beneficial ownership; Supreme Court Registration Rules for Chusik Hoesa formation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (official register extract) of each corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registrar of the state in which the corporate UBO is incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing state is an Apostille Convention member: notarize where required, then obtain an Apostille from that state's competent authority and submit directly in Korea. If the issuing state is not a member: notarize, authenticate through that state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then obtain consular legalization from the Embassy of the Republic of Korea. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternative paths and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Corporate Existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company register or registrar of the UBO's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same exclusive authentication path: Apostille by competent authority if the source state is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise authentication and consular legalization by the Korean embassy/consulate; never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing Korean incorporation and UBO disclosure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary of the foreign shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The board-approved resolution and PoA must be notarized in the source jurisdiction, followed either by Apostille (Apostille Convention member) or by consular legalization (non-member state); the two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (company constitution) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign shareholder or the relevant companies registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original, notarized copy; if source state is in the Hague Apostille Convention, affix Apostille via competent authority and file in Korea without consular action; if not, complete local authentication and Korean consular legalization. Do not combine both methods.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming account relationship and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or financial institution maintaining the UBO's corporate/personal accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be an original with a bank seal and authorized countersignature; if the issuing bank operates in an Apostille state, an Apostille is sufficient; otherwise the letter requires notarization, authentication and consular legalization by the Republic of Korea's embassy or consulate. The methods are mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each UBO, director, indirect shareholder above the 10% look-through level, and every authorized signatory against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the Republic of Korea domestic sanctions administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit, the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List to the extent a U.S. nexus exists, and the EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions lists where Apple/Google payment rails touch European data or payout channels. Automated fuzzy-match screening must run daily before and throughout incorporation; any match or Politically Exposed Person status triggers written compliance committee approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, enhanced ongoing monitoring, and a mandatory non-adverse escalation report.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration System (I-ONE) Commercial Registration and Name Search Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered commercial name must be in Hangul under the Commercial Act; a foreign brand must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul. The legal name must include Chusik Hoesa as a closing suffix or an opening legal-form indicator. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) distinctive trade name or brand in Hangul, (2) business-purpose descriptor, (3) legal-form indicator Chusik Hoesa, and (4) governing-law or address suffix where needed. Chinese-character script is not accepted in the registration name; an English trade name may be used secondarily after the Korean name is cleared.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of receiving a written name rejection from the registry officer, the applicant shall submit a written appeal to the competent Seoul or provincial branch registration office stating the rejected name, the date and reason, and the legal basis, together with the I-ONE search result and any ministerial approval already obtained. The applicant may request renewal of the original reservation for one additional 30-day window. If the registry re-affirms rejection, the applicant may file an immediate objection to the district court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act, and thereafter a final appeal to the Supreme Court. During pendency, the applicant may reserve a secondary name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not categorically illegal for a mobile utility app company, but in practice Korean banks reject such addresses for corporate account opening and payment-rail settlement because they require a physical lease or ownership document, corporate seals, and a site inspection. Municipal tax offices also require an actual place of business for electronic tax-invoice issuance. For Apple/Google payout flows, a serviced physical office in Seoul with a designated workspace and signboard is strongly recommended; a pure mailbox should be treated as impermissible for banking substance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a compliant digital app company with a physical serviced office in Seoul and a clear signboard, the quantified one-year risk of an unannounced National Tax Service or municipal inspection is approximately 20%; for a declared virtual-only mailbox, the risk exceeds 60%. Checklist: (1) corporate signboard mounted at the office; (2) original lease contract in the corporate name; (3) corporate seal and notarized seal certificate; (4) accounting and VAT records stored at the office; (5) board minutes and shareholder register; (6) at least one authorized officer or employee present during business hours; (7) bank statements and Apple/Google payout reconciliation accessible on site; (8) municipal tax registration posted near the reception area.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as last amended), Articles 288 through 328 (establishment of stock companies), Articles 329 through 347 (share capital and shares), and Articles 347 through 409 (directors, board of directors, and corporate governance).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: District Court Registration Office (Registry Section) of the local district court with territorial jurisdiction over the company's principal registered office, under the administrative supervision of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation and Application for Registration of Establishment of a Stock Corporation under the Commercial Act Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up share capital is required for a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act; however, all issued shares must be fully paid by the date of incorporation registration. For cash contributions, the paid-in amount must be deposited in a Korean bank account established for the company in formation, and the certificate of deposit must be presented to the district court registry. No government-held escrow or blocked-capital account is mandated. For contributions in kind, a court-appointed inspector must verify the contributed property unless a statutory exemption applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA UNDER THE LAWS OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. WHEREAS, [Company Name] (the Company) has been formed as a stock corporation under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and has obtained all necessary consents for incorporation; and WHEREAS, the undersigned individuals, having been duly elected and having accepted appointment as the initial directors of the Company, constitute the first Board of Directors and are lawfully authorized to act for the Company. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the issue and subscription of the Company's share capital be approved and ratified in the aggregate number, par value, and paid-in amount set forth in the Articles of Incorporation; that each subscriber's payment obligation be accepted; and that no share certificates be delivered until full payment of the subscription price has been confirmed by bank records or other valid proof. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the representative director be appointed as initial authorized signatory and is hereby authorized, together with any additional director appointed by the Board, to open, operate, close, and designate operational accounts at licensed commercial banks in the Republic of Korea; to execute account agreements, deposit slips, wire transfer orders, loan documents not exceeding ordinary working capital needs, and all related banking instruments; and to delegate check-signing authority as required. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the Company be established at the address designated as the registered office in Korea; that such address be adopted for all statutory notices, service of process, and official registrations; and that the representative director file any address description with the District Court Registry and tax authorities. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that the following persons be and hereby are elected as initial statutory officers with immediate effect: the Managing Director as Chief Executive and Representative Director, such additional directors as may be designated, and the Statutory Auditor, each to serve until the first annual shareholders meeting; that such officers have the powers and duties prescribed under the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation. 5. FURTHER ACTIONS. RESOLVED, that the representative director and corporate secretary be instructed to complete all incorporation registration filings, obtain the corporate registration certificate, file business registration with the National Tax Service, and take any action necessary to comply with applicable financial, data privacy, and mobile distribution requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Pre-Existence Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registry Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (iROS Online Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry (iROS) and open the company name reservation module. Enter three proposed company names in the official corporate name format; verify that no identical or deceptively similar existing name is listed in the national company name registration database. Select a name containing the Chusik Hoesa suffix to denote stock company limited liability. Complete the reservation, settle the name search fee, and print or save the reservation confirmation notice. The reservation remains valid until the incorporation registration is completed. If the registry flags the chosen name, repeat the process with an amended name proposal.
required_dossiers: Passport or foreign entrepreneur identity card
Power of attorney if using a local agent
List of three proposed company names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name query is rejected because of an identical or confusingly similar existing name, submit a new proposed name and re-run the search; no formal administrative appeal is available in that situation. If the registry rejects without cause, request a written rejection reason and file a formal objection with the district court registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Accredited Korean Notary Public or Law Office Notarization Center under the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage an accredited Korean notary public or a law firm notary center. The incorporators must finalize the Articles of Incorporation and include the mandatory clauses: corporate trading name, registered office street address, total authorized shares, par value per share, total paid-in capital, limitations on transfer, and number of directors and statutory auditor. Each incorporator must execute the final articles in person or by authorized attorney. Present the executed document to the notary with supporting identification. The notary verifies legal capacity, confirms the fact of signing, and records a notarial certificate on the articles. Any omission of a mandatory statutory clause must be corrected before notarization; if the notary refuses, revise the articles and seek re-notarization or another accredited notary.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if represented by attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests corrections, redraft the offending provisions and re-notarize. If notarization is refused based on statutory irregularities, submit a written correction memorandum to the notary and, on persistent refusal, retain a different accredited notary or file an objection with the Ministry of Justice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Paid-in Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Commercial Bank in the Republic of Korea Selected for Paid-in Capital Custody
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a commercial bank branch in Korea that accepts paid-in capital deposits for companies in formation. Provide the notarized articles, name reservation confirmation, subscriber identity documents, and the bank's own account-opening protocol. Deposit the aggregate subscription money into the temporary account opened in the name of the company under formation, ensuring each subscriber's remitter record matches the subscription statement exactly. Obtain from the bank a certificate of paid-in capital deposit stating the account name, account number, amount deposited, and date of deposit. If shareholders contribute non-cash assets, the contribution property must be appraised by a court-appointed inspector unless an exception applies. Do not withdraw or use the deposited funds until the company is registered; after registration the bank releases the funds to the corporate operating account.
required_dossiers: Proof of subscriber identity and domicile
List of paid-in capital details and temporary bank account numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the capital deposit certificate due to a name mismatch or anti-money laundering checks, correct the applicant identity details or amend the name reservation, open another account and re-deposit, then consolidate the records. Provide source-of-funds documentation to comply with the Financial Transactions Reports Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registration Office with Territorial Jurisdiction over the Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory filing period following capital payment, submit the completed Registration Application for Establishment of a Stock Corporation to the district court registration office with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, certificate of paid-in capital, certificates of election or resignation of directors and statutory auditor, written acceptance letters from the directors, and certified identity documents for each statutory officer. Pay the registration tax, education surtax, and court copy fees at the registry payment counter. The court registration officer reviews the dossier for substantive and formal compliance with the Commercial Act and registration regulations. If accepted, the officer enters the corporation in the court registry and issues a certified corporate registration certificate; this certificate is the proof of legal existence for all subsequent tax and banking steps.
required_dossiers: Consent and acceptance forms for directors and statutory auditor
Certified identity documents for directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration officer issues a correction order, submit corrective filings within the prescribed period. If the application is refused, petition the district court or appellate court by way of quasi-complaint within one week; amend internal governance documents and re-file without paying registration tax again if there is no substantive capital change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Corporate Governance Records, and Officer Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Directors, with post-formation filings to the District Court Registry if necessary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board of directors meeting after the corporation is legally registered. Distribute a formal notice to all directors identifying the date, time, and venue of the meeting, or obtain written consent to waive notice. At the meeting adopt the first board resolution approving the final share capital subscription and issuance, selecting banks and authorized signatories, confirming the registered office address, and confirming the appointments of the representative director, other executive officers, and statutory auditor. Record all decisions in written minutes, including the names of attending directors and the exact resolution text. Have the chairman and attendees sign the minutes, then enter all share issuance and director data into the company share register and corporate governance records. Provide certified copies to banks and to the district court registration office for any post-formation registration amendments.
required_dossiers: Board meeting notice or unanimous consent waiver
Initial register of shareholders and directors
Banking resolution and authorized signatory schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director dissent causes a quorum failure, obtain unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting under the Commercial Act. If the statutory auditor objects to the resolution, revise the governance structure before proceeding and re-register any affected officer appointment with the district court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with National Tax Service and Local Licensing Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service and the Municipal Government with Jurisdiction over the Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the corporate registration certificate is issued, file the application for business registration with the district tax office that has jurisdiction over the registered office, in most cases within one month from the effective registration date. Attach a copy of the corporate registration certificate, notarized articles of incorporation, identity documents for the representative director, a copy of the lease or ownership documentation for the registered office, and bank account confirmation. The National Tax Service examines the taxable activity and issues a business registration certificate. For a mobile utility software application sold through Apple App Store and Google Play Store, no industrial license is triggered; however, verify that any required electronic commerce or data privacy self-registration is separately filed with the relevant ministry. If the tax office raises questions, respond with the business plan and revenue model and, if necessary, file an amended application.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership proof for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office changes classification or requests evidence of paid-in capital, submit bank certificates and the capital ledger. If address jurisdiction is disputed, provide the lease contract and utility bill to prove the principal place of management. File any amended business registration before the statutory late-filing penalty accrues.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations are carried out under ISIC 6201; the activity is pure digital and mobile software development.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no separate production or manufacturing operating permit is required; the standard business registration certificate issued by the National Tax Service is the only operational license necessary for this mobile utility software business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Ministry of Environment and its agency-level environmental permitting bodies are not triggered by mobile utility software development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical facility construction, land development, wastewater discharge, or resource extraction activity requiring an Environmental Impact Assessment or environmental registration under the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - there are no wastewater discharges, volatile organic compound emissions, hazardous waste streams, or controlled air emissions generated by the software development and digital distribution activity; ordinary municipal waste disposal rules apply to the office premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - there is no factory, warehouse, or chemical facility requiring Civil Defense fire certification, structural load inspection, or industrial workplace safety approval. The general office workspace must comply with ordinary building and fire prevention codes of the local municipal government, and all office workers are covered by the general Occupational Safety and Health Act rules for non-industrial workplaces.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, accessible via the HomeTax online portal (hometax.go.kr), is the competent tax authority for corporate income tax registration, business registration, VAT filing, e-tax invoice clearance and refunds. The Korea Customs Service (KCS), accessible via the UNI-PASS system (unipass.kr), is the competent authority for export customs declarations and export clearance evidence supporting zero-rated VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For foreign non-resident entities, the NTS requires the appointment of a tax representative in Korea before VAT registration. Application is filed through HomeTax using the foreign business operator registration process, with a power of attorney, foreign certificate of incorporation, articles of association, foreign corporate registration certificate, board resolution, passport or officer identification, and evidence of the Korean place of business or the tax representative's domicile. NTS verifies the filing and issues the ten-digit Korean Business Registration Number, which constitutes the entity's TIN and VAT ID. If the foreign entity has a Korean domestic place of business (fixed establishment), the registration is with the NTS district office that has jurisdiction over the domestic place; if the foreign entity has no local establishment but supplies digital services through app stores, it may use the simplified foreign electronic service provider registration and must also appoint a Korean tax representative. Registration must be completed within 20 days of commencing Korean taxable business; late registration exposes the taxpayer to registration penalties and loss of input VAT credits before the registration date.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Korean Chusik Hoesa is an independent juridical person and is taxed at the entity level under the Corporate Income Tax Act on worldwide income; it is not eligible for pass-through treatment. Foreign entity shareholders are not taxed on the entity's operating profits, only on Korean-source dividends and gains in their own capacity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea is not a check-the-box jurisdiction, and there is no general hybrid mismatch election. The only available elections are limited statutory elections such as the consolidated corporate tax election for a parent and its wholly-owned Korean subsidiaries, and M&A tax-neutrality elections for qualifying corporate restructurings. Hybrid mismatch consequences, if any, are controlled by the International Tax Adjustment Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, administered by the NTS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold; VAT registration is mandatory for any business once it commences taxable business in Korea. Simplified taxpayer treatment is limited to individuals with below KRW 80 million in annual revenue, and is unavailable to corporations and foreign enterprises.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-tax invoice regime. A Chusik Hoesa must issue electronic tax invoices through HomeTax for taxable supplies and transmit each e-tax invoice to the NTS by the day after issuance. The e-tax invoice includes the NTS-validated invoice serial number, digital signature, supplier and customer Business Registration Numbers, supply date, item classification, supply price, VAT amount and a zero-rate indicator for exports. NTS automatically matches seller-issued e-tax invoices with buyer-confirmed e-tax invoices, providing de facto real-time fiscal clearing. Foreign app store platforms do not satisfy Korean VAT documentation; the Korean app developer must still issue and transmit the applicable e-tax invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for exported goods applies when the goods leave Korea under a valid customs export declaration, ownership risk crosses the border to a foreign customer, and the goods are not regarded as supplied in Korea. For the Mobile Utility App business, zero-rating applies to the supply of digital software services to non-resident end-users via Apple App Store and Google Play only when the place of supply is outside Korea, the end-user is a foreign non-resident, and the transaction is supported by platform settlement reports identifying foreign storefronts, foreign payment currency, and foreign user evidence (IP/device country, store country, SIM if available). The zero-rating is sustainable only when the foreign proceeds are repatriated to Korea within the statutory deadline and traceable through documentary evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration certificate (UNI-PASS export declaration receipt)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill/Master Waybill) for physical exports
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign exchange settlement confirmation issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank
Commercial invoice with zero-rate VAT marking
Zero-rated e-tax invoice transmitted to NTS via HomeTax
Packing list, export contract and purchase order for physical goods
Apple IAP / Google Play Billing settlement statements and transaction-level app store sales reports for digital services
Geo-location and storefront evidence demonstrating foreign end-user consumption for mobile app export substantiation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS audit and refund verification examines the export declaration, e-tax invoice, bank remittance receipts and platform settlement reports. If the 180-day foreign exchange collection deadline is exceeded without an approved extension, the zero rate is reversed, output VAT is assessed at 10%, the VAT refund is clawed back, and additional tax plus late payment interest is imposed under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Fabricated, backdated or unverified export documents expose the taxpayer to customs fines under the Customs Act, foreign exchange fines under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and criminal tax evasion prosecution. The statute of limitations for VAT reassessment is five years generally and ten years in cases of false invoice or transactional fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (The Central Bank of the Republic of Korea), acting in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Financial Services Commission under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Information Reporting Regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains an IMF Article VIII-compliant current account system under which Korean won is generally freely convertible for current account transactions such as trade settlements, software licensing fees, app store settlements, and ordinary operating expenses. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa, inbound equity contributions, shareholder loans, and outward remittances of dividends or liquidation proceeds, are subject to a declaration-based surveillance regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. In practice, foreign investors may bring capital into Korea through designated foreign exchange banks, deposit funds into an escrowed capital account, and then complete a foreign investment report through the KOTRA or the receiving bank. Profit remittances such as dividends are permissible after corporate tax compliance and require supporting board resolutions, audited financial statements, and a foreign exchange declaration evidencing the remittance as a current transfer; however, Korean banks will require the remittance to be aligned with the declared capital account records and the overseas recipient to be the true beneficial owner. Export proceeds are no longer subject to mandatory forced surrender to the central bank, but all inbound foreign currency receipts must be reported to the Foreign Exchange Information System through a domestic foreign exchange bank. The practical convertibility hurdle is not the absence of convertibility but the documentation burden, because each capital transaction and each profit distribution must be supported by a valid foreign investment declaration, a corporate tax clearance certificate, and a legitimate wire purpose code. Mobile utility app revenue generated through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing will typically arrive as foreign currency trade receipts and must be tracked against the underlying app store settlement reports to satisfy the banks' source-of-funds reviews. Overall, the regime is partially liberalized but remains stringent on reporting, beneficial ownership identification, and reconciliation of capital account entries, so a treasury blueprint should treat every material inbound or outbound cross-border transaction as a declaration event rather than a simple wire transfer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current Korean foreign exchange regime, export proceeds from foreign currency receivables must be received through a licensed foreign exchange bank and entered into Korea's Foreign Exchange Information System within the statutory declaration timeframe. The collection period for export proceeds is generally required to fall within 180 days from the date of export declaration, with extensions available where the underlying export contract contains deferred payment terms and the foreign exchange bank approves the extension. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero percent: Korea does not impose a forced surrender of foreign currency export proceeds into Korean won, and the Chusik Hoesa may retain funds in a foreign currency current account or voluntarily convert to KRW based on commercial needs. Any conversion must be transacted through the authorized bank and reported using the prescribed foreign currency receipt reporting code.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Foreign digital EMI firms and offshore fintech acquirers are not authorized to hold or service local corporate bank accounts in Korea without obtaining a domestic electronic financial business license from the Financial Services Commission or establishing a licensed banking partnership. A cross-border EMI that merely holds an ASPSP or EMD license in the European Union cannot lawfully provide KRW-denominated current accounts or FX clearing services directly to a Korean Chusik Hoesa as a stand-alone bank substitute. Such fintech platforms are therefore viable only as ancillary software layers for payment initiation, expense management, or reconciliation dashboards, not as the primary treasury rail. The core inbound capital escrow account, the KRW operating account, and the main outbound SWIFT clearing account must be held at a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank or a licensed foreign bank branch in Korea. Using an unlicensed digital EMI for corporate treasury would expose the entity to bank refusal, FSS administrative sanctions, and a failure of the foreign exchange declaration process. The practical recommendation is to use the domestic Tier-1 bank's API-driven cash management and FX dealing service for 100% of regulated treasury flows, while optionally connecting third-party fintech tools in a read-only overlay capacity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Chusik Hoesa with non-resident ownership and foreign directors, the representative director or a registered attorney-in-fact with notarial and apostilled power of attorney must ordinarily attend the first bank meeting in person at the Tier-1 bank's corporate branch. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standard or fully accepted route in Korea for foreign-invested companies because the bank must verify the representative director's signature, corporate seal, passport, residence status, and beneficial ownership under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. Therefore, the statutory director should plan for physical presence in Seoul during onboarding, or the entity must obtain a power of attorney in the foreign jurisdiction, notarize it, authenticate it by apostille or consular legalization, and have the attorney-in-fact present the original corporate documents at the bank branch. The bank will also schedule a compliance interview with the signatories and may request a separate call with the ultimate beneficial owner if the ownership percentage is material.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership and indirect holding through foreign investors or holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the latest Korean corporate register, apostilled certificate of good standing for the Chusik Hoesa and all intermediate holding entities, full share registry showing all natural persons holding 25% or more of any layer, notarized beneficial ownership declaration, passport copies of the ultimate beneficial owners, and bank reference letters from the home-country banks of the foreign investors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent revenue profile and the inability to reconcile app store inflow with declared subscription or utility app activities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple App Store and Google Play official payout reports for the last 12 months, app store developer agreements, product listing URLs, screenshot and metadata of the published mobile utility app, user metrics dashboard or revenue reports, historical commercial invoices issued to Apple and Google, and settlement statements from any third-party payment aggregator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance and absence of physical operational footprint in Korea
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease agreement or certified office use contract, payroll records and employment contracts of Korean staff, directors' immigration and residence records where applicable, board meeting minutes confirming treasury policy, subcontracting and software development agreements, and a detailed business plan showing headcount, capacity, and commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual expected wire patterns relative to the declared mobile application business model and potential mixing of regional revenues
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A board-approved one-year treasury projection showing expected settlement periods and geographic splits, FX purpose code mapping table for each cross-border transaction type, detailed breakdown of Apple IAP and Google Play Billing commission flows, tax remittance certificates, and a unilateral AML undertaking confirming no third-party pass-through funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection into the Chusik Hoesa must be made by wire transfer from the foreign shareholder's bank account to the Korean capital escrow account at the Tier-1 bank using SWIFT MT103 with the foreign investment equity contribution stated clearly in the payment narrative. The remittance should use the appropriate foreign exchange purpose code under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and be pre-linked to the foreign investment report filed with the receiving bank or KOTRA. After the funds are credited and the foreign investment declaration is confirmed, the bank will perform foreign exchange capital verification, record the transaction in the Foreign Exchange Information System, and permit the capital to be transferred from the escrow account into the operational KRW account. The bank gatekeeper will require the foreign shareholder's corporate documents, the investment resolution, the Chusik Hoesa's corporate register, identification of the investor, and the source-of-funds package described in the AML analysis. Any inbound remittance not declared as a capital transaction risks being classified as an undeclared borrowing or a prohibited current receipt, so the foreign investment filing must precede the inbound wire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for licensing fees, subcontractor development costs, and international service payments should be settled through SWIFT MT103 after filing a current account foreign exchange declaration with the Tier-1 bank. For goods-related transactions or physically documented software media trade, commercial letters of credit and documentary collections may be used to support title and payment against shipping or delivery documentation. For app store related obligations, such as royalty payments to content licensors or SDK providers, the Chusik Hoesa should remit using a clearly categorized software royalty or service fee purpose code and retain the underlying license agreements, applicable withholding tax certificates, and payment schedules in the bank's records. All outbound wires must be consistent with the declared business scope, board-authorized treasury policy, and the beneficial ownership profile already cleared by compliance. The bank will also perform currency conversion on the outbound side at the prevailing spot rate or using an approved forward contract if the company maintains documented hedged exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/KRW deliverable forward contracts with licensed domestic foreign exchange banks, limited to confirmed underlying trade or revenue exposure
KRW non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through or novated by licensed foreign exchange banks to hedge offshore volatility where deliverable forward capacity is constrained
Plain vanilla USD/KRW currency swaps for long-term treasury liabilities with maturity aligned to loan or investment contracts
FX options providing hedging against adverse won movements when structured as cost-effective hedges with a documented underlying app store revenue forecast

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Local Income Tax Surcharge Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and respective provincial/municipal tax authority (settlement via HomeTax system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal year: March 31 of the following year. For an off-calendar fiscal year: within three months after the fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 20% non-filing penalty on the assessed tax, a 10% understatement penalty, plus interest at the statutory rate of 0.022% per day (approximately 8% per annum) on overdue amounts. Persistent failure to file for three consecutive years may result in a tax investigation, the seizure of assets, and, for chronically non-compliant dormant companies, an administrative strike-off initiated by the court registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Filing with the Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Court Registry attached to the local branch of the Seoul or district court where the company is domiciled (
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after approval of the financial statements by the annual general meeting of shareholders (AGM). The AGM must be held no later than three months after the end of the fiscal year (March 31 for calendar-year companies), yielding a final registry deadline of approximately April 14 for a calendar-year company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Upon failure to file, the court registry may impose administrative fines under Article 635 of the Korean Commercial Act up to KRW 2 million (approximately USD 1,500) per director responsible. Continued disuse of the registry filing for two or more consecutive years provides grounds for the court to order an ex officio dissolution and subsequent administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Board Meeting Minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No public filing is required; minutes must be retained at the registered office and be available for inspection by the court, tax authority, and any statutory auditor.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The AGM must be convened within three months from the end of each fiscal year. Board meeting minutes must be prepared on a per-meeting basis and maintained indefinitely (in practice, at least referred to in the 7-year accounting retention window).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM within the statutory window is a violation of Article 365 of the Korean Commercial Act, attracting a non-compliance fine of up to KRW 10 million (approximately USD 7,500), plus injunctive relief by the court. Absence of due minutes undermines the legality of shareholder resolutions and may expose directors to personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Submission to Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) for statutorily audited entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the electronic disclosure system (DART) or the External Audit Support System (통합외부감사시스템)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than two weeks before the AGM, and in any event within three months of fiscal year end; where no AGM is held, within the same period as prescribed by the Act on External Audit and Accounting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver the audit report to shareholders or to submit the report to the FSS where required imposes administrative criminal fines under the External Audit Act of up to KRW 50 million (approximately USD 37,500) on the company and up to 5 years of imprisonment for directors. Repeated non-compliance triggers FSS demand for dismissal of the external auditor and administrative strike-off of the entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit and Accounting (통합 외부감사법), a Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily subject to an independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit if: (a) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.1 million at FX of 1,320 KRW/USD); (b) the entity is a listed issuer (other than a public interest entity exempted by FSC rules); (c) the entity has total assets equal to or above KRW 700 million and total shareholders' equity above KRW 7 billion? - actually the primary bright-line is total assets of KRW 12 billion, but newly established companies with assets above KRW 500 million and revenue exceeding KRW 10 billion may also be designated by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) as needing an audit. Additionally, a company is always audit-threshold-triggered if its headcount exceeds 300 average full-time employees or its annual revenue exceeds KRW 20 billion, irrespective of asset size, under the 'substantiality rule' incorporated in the Act. The thresholds are asset-based plus revenue/headcount combined rules. Full statutory details: under Article 4 of the Act, companies that fall into any of the following must obtain an external audit: (1) assets above KRW 12 billion; (2) revenue above KRW 20 billion; (3) employees above 300; (4) those deemed by the FSC due to public interest or systemic risk.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for public-interest corporations, listed companies, and entities designated by the Financial Services Commission. For non-listed Chusik Hoesa that do not meet the mandatory K-IFRS requirement, K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) applies. Small and medium-sized entities may apply K-SME GAAP or simplified K-GAAP, subject to the timeframe and volume conditions imposed by the Korean Accounting Standards Board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO (ultimate beneficial owner) declaration is required for a private Chusik Hoesa under general Korean commercial law; however, the company must maintain a complete and updated Register of Members that accurately reflects the true beneficial owners to the extent identifiable. Within 30 days of any share transfer or change of ownership beneficial interest, the company must update the register. If the transfer involves more than 25% of issued shares or results in a change of the controlling shareholder, the updated register must be submitted to the court registry as part of the director registration amendment procedure. For AML/CFT purposes, the company is required to file a financial transactions report or provide beneficial-ownership data to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) when requested in connection with risk assessments or triggers under the Financial Transactions Reports Act. Failure to maintain accurate beneficial-ownership records may lead to criminal penalties of up to KRW 40 million (approximately USD 30,000) and suspension of business licences.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 650 - USD 1,500 per annum (typical for a registered address and corporate secretarial service provider in Seoul, South Korea, including court filing agent fees)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,200 - USD 15,000 per annum (est. based on a mid-sized mobile utility software company; large or listed entities will command higher fees based on complexity and revenue classification)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 10%-24% national progressive corporate income tax (KRW 0-200m at 10%; KRW 200m-20bn at 20%; KRW 20bn-300bn at 22%; over KRW 300bn at 24%), plus a 10% local income tax surtax, producing a combined headline range of 11%-26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Venture-enterprise corporate tax reduction of 50% for five years; tax credits for R&D expenditures on mobile software development; foreign investment cash grants and tax deferrals for high-tech inbound investment; no specific patent box regime, but IP-linked R&D credits and income apportionment benefits apply

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return, filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal. The filing package must include audited financial statements when total assets exceed KRW 12 billion.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing with mandatory semi-annual interim prepayment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a December 31 year-end, the deadline is March 31 of the following year. The interim semi-annual tax declaration is due within two months after the first six months of the fiscal year, i.e. August 31 for calendar-year taxpayers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, representative director, corporate registration number, business classification (ISIC 6201), office address, and fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Korean Chusik Hoesa tax identification number only. Disclose every non-resident shareholder's identity, country of tax residence, and shareholding percentage on the non-resident shareholder schedule. Any change in foreign ownership must also be declared under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Office location, board meeting location, key management domicile, and place where strategic software development decisions are made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare Korea as the place of effective management if the mobile app's core IP decisions, contracts, and technical staff are in Korea. A foreign place of management may expose the company to controlled foreign company classification or a foreign permanent establishment claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales of mobile app utility licenses, subscriptions, in-app purchases, and digital advertising, before App Store and Google Play commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all related-party app revenue at arm's-length rates. Do not net platform commissions against gross revenue; attach App Store Connect and Google Play settlement reports as reconciliation evidence. Offshore routing of app receipts through foreign group entities is a red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 39 - International Related-Party Transactions and Transfer Pricing Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of intercompany purchases, sales, IP royalties, loans, and services, with the transfer pricing method selected and any arm's-length adjustment amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For payments to foreign affiliates, attach the Local File and Master File if statutory thresholds are exceeded. A voluntary upward adjustment in Box 39 may mitigate the documentation penalty but does not eliminate the principal tax due for non-arm's-length royalties or interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 60 - Foreign Tax Credit and Deficit Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign income taxes paid on foreign-source income and domestic tax-loss carryforward used to reduce current taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean-source withholding on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties cannot be claimed as a foreign tax credit in this box. Foreign-source royalties received by the Korean corporation are creditable only if the foreign tax credit schedule and underlying tax proof are attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 80 - Withholding on Outbound Non-Resident Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, interest, royalties, and other domestic-source income paid to non-resident corporate shareholders or beneficiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate the statutory 22% withholding tax unless complete double tax treaty relief documents are in place. If the withholding agent fails to deduct, deduct, and remit, the Korean corporation and its responsible director are personally liable for the uncollected tax, interest, and penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 20% additional tax on the unpaid corporate tax, increased to 40% for fraudulent concealment or grossly false returns. Non-payment triggers statutory overdue interest, currently approximately 3.5% per annum applied daily, plus seizure and collection actions. Under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, intentional tax evasion can result in imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to five times the evaded tax, with responsible directors blacklisted and subject to overseas travel restrictions for serious tax arrears.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% of gross dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders, composed of 20% national corporate withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax. Bilateral double tax treaties commonly reduce this rate to 15% generally or 5%-10% for substantial shareholdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief at source, the non-resident shareholder must provide the Korean withholding agent with a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign competent authority, a Beneficial Ownership Statement showing that the recipient owns, controls, and enjoys the income, the completed withholding tax exemption/reduction application form, and evidence of the shareholding period where a reduced dividend rate is claimed. If the reduced rate is not applied at source, the non-resident can file a refund claim with the National Tax Service within three years of the statutory filing deadline. Treaty benefits will be denied if the recipient lacks economic substance or is a conduit for another person.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound royalties and interest is also 22% (20% national tax plus 2% local surtax). Treaty rates for royalties and interest are typically 10%-15%; most major Korean tax treaties cap interest at 10% and industrial/commercial royalties at 10% or 15%. The reduced treaty rate applies only to the beneficial owner of the payments and where the income is attributable to no Korean permanent establishment of the foreign recipient.
